newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae defends plan against dissenter.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae defends plan against dissenter.

text.p: The Student Loan Marketing Association said on Friday a company director, who has protested against its plan to restructure into a private corporation, had not put forward any better alternatives.

The association, better known as Sallie Mae, said earlier its board had approved a plan to restructure as a fully private, federally-chartered corporation. Sallie Mae is the nation's largest source of college-education financing.
Albert Lord, a Sallie Mae director, said he and other directors voted against the plan. He said he agreed that Sallie Mae should be privated but disagreed with the plan.

"We were surprised by Lord's comments, in tone and tenor," Sallie Mae Executive Vice President and General Counsel Tim Greene said. "He has not brought forward to the board an alternative plan of reorganization or an effective business plan."

Lord said he and seven other directors voted against the proposed reorganisation plan, including the board's decision not to name six of the existing shareholder-elected directors to the proposed new board.
Sallie Mae said its plan included an 18-member board of directors, comprised of 10 members who have either served or are serving as directors and eight new nominees.

"Management has put forward a powerful privatization initiative which will increase shareholder value," Greene said. "The only plan we've seen recently from Lord is one that would give him control of the company and this notion will not prevail with this board."
